plan.scope: offline synthetic validation; no native binary/provider permission

test_duration_basis: Runner seconds use time.monotonic, not the continuous admission clock. They are not capture-to-reservation measurements or evidence of a quiet, unsuspended host.

admission.mechanism: 900 seconds, as assigned: the earlier timing evidence lacks a measured admission interval that supports a different value. The bound starts at execute_child entry and ends at the dispatch origin on the existing suspension-inclusive elapsed clock. It consumes none of the 900, 21600 or 43200 child seconds. A 0.1-second periodic POSIX alarm checks that clock and raises AdmissionExpired through interruptible Python syscalls; the exception bypasses broad Exception handlers. A synchronous check at dispatch refuses an expired bound even before alarm delivery. Signal ownership is exclusive and restored after admission. Existing controller cleanup, keep-awake cleanup and failure publication retain the distinct reason: native admission deadline elapsed; child was not dispatched. Cleanup/publication themselves lie outside the admission interval.
admission.limitations: This in-process mechanism cannot preempt an uninterruptible kernel call or a C extension that never services Python signals; alarm handling resumes when the host and Python run again. The exact dispatch check remains fail-closed. Earlier pre-reservation verification is outside this timer. The real FIFO-open tests exercise interruptible syscall cancellation, not a universal hard-real-time cleanup guarantee.

capture_timing: The new host-pre-dispatch-<registration-sha256>.jsonl lives beside the attempt, outside the closed capture tree. Timestamps are buffered until a freshly verified registration supplies the canonical existing parent. Explicit capture, current guard preparation and public launch scopes append capture observation, current_guard_preparation, every active registration.verified call, admission with classifier, controller construction/prewarm, _current_authority and reservation start/end, plus attempt_reserved. The synthetic fixture records its invented capture at minting. Step IDs, trace IDs, process IDs and registration digest join rows; capture timestamps/digests distinguish captures. It uses the same continuous clock and is never read for admission. It stops after reservation. Byte/row buffering is bounded; failed/contended writes disable observation. Missing rows mean unknown timing. Synchronous diagnostic I/O can add latency; it is not claimed to have zero runtime effect. No newly instrumented public duration is claimed before pins are admitted.
capture_reordering_proposal_only: A later capture is possible in principle without changing the 1200-second maximum age or 300-second margin. Source-only registration, review/word/protocol validation, classifier derivation and controller prewarm do not need the captured quota event. _current_authority reconstructs those inputs; its quota request validation does not inspect an observed event. Current guard preparation and latest-claim selection do need the capture and cannot simply move before it. Proposed for the lead: a reviewed preparation phase finishes cold source/controller work, then takes one fresh capture, constructs its current guard, rechecks exact source/input identities and the current word/latest claim under the existing lock, and reserves. Keep all final freshness, source, word and dispatch checks; do not reuse a previously verified value as launch authority. Current consumer-loader scopes cannot simply be held across bootstrap orchestration. Measure the remaining fresh reconstruction before promising that it fits 900 seconds. This needs an explicit two-phase interface/source review; no reordering, retimestamping, recapture or limit relaxation was implemented.
